paragraphs.source_en: Such decoherence, as it is called, is necessary if a system is to behave 98 • Chapter 5 - Hawking in a classical manner rather than a quantum one. People normally try to account for decoherence by interactions with an external system, such as a heat bath, that is not measured. In the case of the universe there is no external system, but I would suggest that the reason we observe classical behavior is that we can see only part of the universe. One might think that at late times one would be able to see all the universe and the event horizon would disappear. But this is not the case. The no-boundary proposal implies that the universe is spatially closed. A closed universe will collapse again before an observer has time to see all the universe.
